unit_j_basis: EXPLORATORY scan at X = 50000 (explore): trace/prime r is maximal for j in {0, 3}
classes: RS-S015 singles: pi^k, k = 1..5, over the 20 smallest primary primes (k1.classes singles)

settings.prime: columns = split primes sigma, N <= X, trace-normalized G
settings.unrestricted: columns = all squarefree primary c coprime to 6 (split and inert factors), N(c) <= X, trace-normalized G by twisted multiplicativity

statistic: s = eps * N6^(1/6), eps = (r^2 - 1)/(r_1^2 - 1), r_1 = kappa = 1 vector in the same setting

predictions.text: B = mean s over pi^5 singles with t >= 3 (prime setting), U = same (unrestricted). If B > -0.6: BASELINE_ABSENT. Else SIEVE_SUPPORTED if U - B >= 0.5 or U > 0; INTRINSIC if |U - B| <= 0.25; otherwise UNDECIDED. The reviewer-suggested sieve hypothesis predicts SIEVE_SUPPORTED.

In each setting, plateau Pl = mean s over k in {1..4} singles with t <= 1e-2, crossover C = mean s over k in {1..4} singles with 10^-0.5 <= t <= 10^0.5. PROFILE_PRESENT iff Pl in [0.5, 1.3] and C <= Pl - 0.3. Predicted: PRESENT in both settings (crossover is a shift-aspect property of the Gauss-sum first moment); ABSENT in the unrestricted setting would make it prime-specific.

power_note: Class counts at X = 2e5: P uses 15 pi^5 singles (N = 19..73); Q plateau 38 classes, crossover 11 classes (k = 3, N = 43..73; k = 4, N = 19, 25). Random-phase sd of r about 0.003 at D ~ 1.8e4, so sigma_eps ~ 0.007 and sigma_s(pi^5) ~ 0.08-0.25 per class; SE of B, U about 0.05.
